A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, three MDP diagrams, construction tables, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical guarantees, lower-bound constructions, and proofs, including in its appendices. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper. Its MDP examples and appendices provide mathematical constructions and proofs, without empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the clipping/penalty parameter from α/(n(s,a)−1) to α/max{n(s,a)−1,1}, fixing its definition for small sample counts. The value-iteration procedure, discount choice, and policy extraction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on empirical datasets or benchmarks. The theoretical MDP settings and lower-bound examples are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. The analytical comparison with Ozdaglar et al. (2024) is unchanged; newly cited methods are discussed only as related work.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. The revised clipping parameter is an algorithmic correction, not a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies are added or removed. The mathematical hard examples and supporting theoretical analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probability guarantees are theoretical and retain their stated levels.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are introduced or revised, and the main analytical bounds and lower-bound findings remain unchanged. Figure 2's corrected labels depict the transition probabilities already specified in v1's construction.

T1.justification: The revised definition of β is propagated through Appendix B, including Lemmas B.7 and B.8 and the span analysis. Added steps justify replacing max{n−1,1} by n−1 under the existing sample-count conditions. The main theorem statements, rates, and lower-bound constructions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the claims of fully single-policy guarantees, applicability to weakly communicating MDPs, necessary transient coverage, and nearly matching lower bounds.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains why the arbitrary default distribution for an unobserved transition row cannot affect the update: quantile clipping forces the minimum-value branch. The interpretations of transient coverage and the stated tabular limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly specifies an empirical transition distribution of 1/S when n(s,a)=0. V1 supplies only the sample-frequency formula, leaving division by zero unresolved. This adds a concrete implementation convention.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds seven references and locally expands discussion of instance-dependent pessimistic bounds and earlier uniform-coverage methods. Examples include Yin and Wang (2021), Yin et al. (2022), and Munos (2007). Existing Zurek–Chen works also receive publication updates.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to related-work paragraphs, the zero-sample explanation and footnote, brief proof clarifications, and bibliographic wording. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 corrects transition labels from 1/p and 1−1/p to p and 1−p, matching the existing construction table. Added text produces modest layout reflow; the same figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 fixes the clipping parameter's zero denominator at n=1, specifies handling of unobserved state-action pairs, and makes Figure 2 consistent with its transition table. These corrections improve implementability and clarity, with additional related-work context. The central guarantees and scientific scope remain stable.
